title: User Intent Variability Probe and Labelling Specification
author: Priya Menon
body:
Summary
-------
This document specifies a repeatable process and annotation contract for generating a 'User Intent Variability' probe dataset used to: (1) stress-test model sensitivity to realistic intent paraphrases, (2) measure degradation under distributional shift, and (3) provide labeled signal for automated regression triage and calibration. The dataset is designed to be compact (5–25k items per workload) and representative of production intent clusters across text-generation and chat features.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all production-facing prompt families used by Redwood-hosted or dedicated deployments (generation, chat, reranking).
- Intended for use in: continuous evals, pre-promotion acceptance checks, canary traffic probes, and regression triage workbooks.
- Not a replacement for broad prompt catalogs; this is a focused probe for intent-level variability and label consistency.

Goals
-----
1. Produce a stable set of intent paraphrase clusters for each workload that capture semantic variation, register (formal/informal), and short-form vs. long-form intent.
2. Define an annotation contract with clear labels and adjudication steps to minimize annotator drift.
3. Provide tooling and sampling recipes so teams can regenerate similar probes for new locales or products.

High-level procedure (overview)
------------------------------
1. Identify seed intents and canonical examples (owner: product / solutions engineering).
2. Automatically expand seeds with paraphrase generators and retrieval from historical telemetry (owner: applied ML).
3. Apply stratified sampling to select examples across frequency, user tier, and input length (owner: applied ML).
4. Human annotation according to the contract below; adjudicate conflicts (owner: annotation ops).
5. Publish dataset artifacts and evaluation scripts to the eval harness and schedule the probe in nightly runs (owner: eval infra).

Seed identification (detailed)
----------------------------
- Responsible party: product manager of the feature + solutions engineering.
- Deliverable: CSV of seed intents with columns: seed_id, canonical_text, feature_route, traffic_pct, notes.
- Minimum: 20 seeds per feature family for small features; 50+ for heavyweight verticals (e.g., knowledge assistants).

Automated expansion recipes
--------------------------
- Paraphrase model stage: Use a controlled paraphraser (quantized Llama-style model or Redwood-curated open model) at temperature 0.2–0.6 to generate N=50 candidates per seed.
- Telemetry retrieval: Pull up to 500 matching historical utterances per seed via fuzzy-match on normalized tokens and intent tags. CLI example: 

  redwood-telemetry export --feature chat-composer --seed-text "summarize my email" --days 90 --max 500 --output seed-telemetry.json

- De-duplication: apply normalization (lowercase, strip punctuation, remove email/URLs, canonicalize numbers) and cluster by Jaccard and cosine on 768-d embeddings. Keep top K per cluster.

Stratified selection procedure
-----------------------------
1. Define strata: frequency quantile (high/med/low), user_tier (free/pro), locale (en-US, en-GB, es-ES), length bucket (short < 20 tokens, medium 20–80, long > 80), and presence_of_sensitive_entities (Y/N).
2. Target per-seed sample size: 40 examples, allocated across strata using the allocation matrix below.

Allocation matrix (example)
| Stratum | Proportion |
|---|---|
| high-frequency, pro | 0.20 |
| high-frequency, free | 0.10 |
| medium-frequency | 0.25 |
| low-frequency (tail) | 0.25 |
| sensitive entities | 0.20 |
| long-form | 0.10 |

(Cells can overlap; normalization should ensure total per-seed ~= 40)

Annotation contract
-------------------
- Annotator skill: workers with 6+ months of conversational labeling experience and passing our calibration test (85% agreement on gold set).
- Labels (primary):
  - intent_match: {exact, partial, different}
  - canonical_slot_map: free-text mapping of top 3 slots (CSV-safe)
  - response_quality_expectation: {good, borderline, bad}
  - ambiguity_flag: {none, ambiguous, needs-context}
- Adjudication: if intent_match disagreement occurs across two annotators, a senior adjudicator performs review and sets final label; provide free-text rationale.
- Annotation UI fields and instructions: include normalization examples, examples of 'partial' vs 'different', and guidance for edge cases (very short utterances, incomplete sentences).

Quality metrics and thresholds
------------------------------
- Inter-annotator agreement (IAA): Cohen's kappa > 0.6 for intent_match on published probes.
- Label stability: when re-annotating a 5% held-out subset after 90 days, intent_match agreement >= 0.85.
- Coverage: for each seed, at least 70% of selected examples must have canonical_slot_map populated for generation features.
- Noise budget: maximum 3% of examples may be flagged as unusable due to PII or scraping errors.

Evaluation runs and metrics to produce
------------------------------------
- Produce the following evaluation artifacts per nightly run:
  - per-seed confusion matrix (model vs. gold intent_match)
  - aggregate intent-specific F1, precision, recall
  - response divergence index (RDI): token-level BLEU/ROUGE against calibrated reference responses for deterministic tasks
  - stability_delta: change in intent_match F1 compared to last promotion baseline

Promotion and gating rules
--------------------------
- Promotion to canary: no regression (stability_delta >= -0.01 absolute F1) on the probe for 3 consecutive nightly runs and IAA > 0.6.
- Promote to production: canary stability within -0.005 F1 and no new critical ambiguity regressions (ambiguity_flag rises > 1.5x).
- Emergency rollback: any release causing a drop > 0.02 absolute F1 or increasing unusable examples > 2x triggers immediate rollback and regression triage.

Integration with regression triage playbooks
------------------------------------------
- The probe's per-example telemetry is linked to the regression triage workbook via stable ids (seed_id + example_hash). When a regression is detected, the triage flow runs automatic clustering over failing examples and emits candidate blame signals: prompt drift, quantization change, runtime kernel change, and model-version delta.
- Include a minimal debug payload with each failing example: request headers, model_version, quant_profile_id, runtime_kernels, latency_ms, and tokenization_map. Example JSON snippet: 

  {
    "seed_id": "s-1024",
    "example_hash": "a1b2c3d4",
    "model_version": "rwd-13b-v2.3",
    "quant_profile": "q8h_s_2026-01",
    "latency_ms": 132,
    "tokens": 48
  }

Tooling and reproducibility
---------------------------
- Store probe artifacts in the eval-harness bucket under: s3://redwood-evals/probes/{feature}/{probe-name}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/
- Required artifact files: probes.csv, gold_labels.csv, annotator_logs.csv, sampling_seed.json, pipeline-config.yaml
- Example pipeline-config.yaml: 

  feature: "chat-composer"
  probe_name: "intent-variability-2026-02"
  seed_source: "product-csv-v2"
  paraphraser_model: "rw-paraphrase-1.0"
  sampling: "stratified"
  annotator_pool: "intent-team-v2"

Scheduling and ownership
------------------------
- Nightly runs: eval infra schedules nightly full-probe evaluation for high-priority features; lightweight weekly runs for low-traffic features.
- Owners: 
  - Product: selects seeds and maintains the seed CSV
  - Applied ML: expansion, sampling, and embedding pipelines
  - Annotation Ops: annotation and adjudication
  - Eval Infra: scheduling, storage, and integration with triage

Appendix A: Example sampling CLI
-------------------------------
- Generate candidate pool:
  redwood-eval pipeline generate-candidates --feature chat-composer --seed-csv seeds.csv --paraphraser rw-paraphrase-1.0 --out candidates.json
- Stratified select:
  redwood-eval sampling stratify --candidates candidates.json --alloc matrix.yaml --out selected.csv

Appendix B: Small reproducible YAML example for local testing
-----------------------------------------------------------
- local-test.yaml:
  feature: "notes-summarize"
  seeds: ["summarize this meeting", "make bullet points"]
  paraphraser: {model: "local-paraphrase-small", n_per_seed: 20}
  sampling: {method: "simple-stratified", strata: ["length", "locale"], per_seed: 15}

Appendix C: Troubleshooting quick checks
----------------------------------------
1. Low IAA: re-run calibration test; increase adjudicator quota; validate gold set freshness.
2. Too many unusable examples: check telemetry export normalization; run PII scrubbing; reduce telemetry lookback window.
3. Unexpected model regressions concentrated on long-form examples: verify tokenization_map and kv-cache length distributions between baseline and candidate models.

Appendix D: Example table — artifact naming conventions
-----------------------------------------------------
| filename | description | required |
|---|---|---|
| probes.csv | list of selected examples with seed mapping | yes |
| gold_labels.csv | final adjudicated labels | yes |
| annotator_logs.csv | per-annotator metadata and times | yes |
| sampling_seed.json | random seed and sampling params | yes |
| pipeline-config.yaml | pipeline runtime config | yes |

References and related pages
----------------------------
- See also: prompt coverage matrix and annotated drift repair guide (link in Related Pages).
- Triage integration: see regression triage playbooks for automated blame signals.
